title: Book One · Chapter 55: A Brown Envelope
story:
It is the day after Ronan's birthday. Mrs Lan finds a brown envelope outside her front room. It is on the little stool under the roof.

Nobody brought it into the room. It is beside her empty shopping basket. One corner is damp. Was it rain? Or a wet hand? The marks do not tell them.

“Were you expecting a letter?” she asks Mum.

Mum wipes her fingers. Then she takes the envelope. “No. I don't know the name on this one.”

The front has a large six. Under it are smaller words. Some writing is grey and unclear at the wet corner. Is that a G at the start of the name? They cannot be sure yet.

“Not Lan,” Mrs Lan says.

Ronan comes to look. He carries Mei's birthday card flat between his hands. He wanted to copy her cat's face. But now he looks at the envelope instead.

“Could it be ours?”

“Your name doesn't begin with G either,” Mum says.

“Maybe for Dad.”

“His name isn't there.”

She turns the envelope over. She does not open it. The flap is stuck down. There is a small HAN at the bottom. Is that the sender's name? Mum does not know yet.

Leo comes to the gate for the map. He sees the envelope in Mum's hand. “Is that birthday money?” he asks.

Ronan looks at the thick middle. Ronan did not think of money before. Now he looks at the thick part again.

“We do not know yet,” Mum says. “The name is not Ronan.”

Mrs Lan takes the envelope to her front room. She puts it on a dry shelf. It is away from the window. She will ask her neighbours about it. Someone left it here. Did anyone see that person? Mum copies the name and address from the front. She keeps the brown envelope with Mrs Lan. The boys do not take it outside.

The moving cart came through this gate nearly half a year ago. Ronan knows many doors now. Which door needs this letter? They do not know yet.

He brings out the street map. The large six at their own gate looks suddenly less useful. Mrs Lan mentioned another six. That address was East Court.

“Could it be that one?” he asks.

“Could be,” Mum says. “That is a question to check.”

Leo points toward the old rice shop. There is a passage behind it. He wants to look there now. Mum says no. Is East Court behind that shop? They do not know. That passage belongs to someone else. They need permission to enter.

The boys sit on the step. Mum shows them her copy. Some letters are clear. The boys copy those. Leo points to another mark. “A T?” he asks. Ronan shakes his head. “It may be part of an E.” They draw both possible letters. They cannot choose one yet.

Mrs Lan visits the neighbour opposite. Then she comes back with a little news. A man stopped at the gate that morning. He had a small parcel. The neighbour was cooking. She did not hear his question. She saw him leave. But she did not see his next stop.

“So we still need his name,” Mrs Lan says.

Ronan wanted a quick answer. Nobody knows the man's name. Nobody can read the whole address. Ronan leaves both questions on the page.

Mum writes a short note. The name is wrong for this house. The envelope is still sealed. They need to ask about HAN. Is it the sender's name? She leaves the note with Mrs Lan.

Before dinner, Ronan puts Mei's card back beside his bed. He looks at the name on its front. His name is clear on his own card. Mei gave it straight to him. This brown envelope needs the right person, too. He leaves it safely with Mrs Lan.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：envelope＝信封；sealed＝封好的；sender＝寄出者；address＝地址。

辅助理解：flap＝信封的封口盖；parcel＝包裹；East Court和West Lane是不同的地址名。

理解问题：

1. Mrs Lan 在哪里发现信封？
2. 大家为什么没有为了寻找线索而拆开它？
